title: Are you guys having the same dilemma??
author: Soft_Cryptographer78
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I’m curious about the daily friction points we all face while building games. Whether you're a solo indie dev or working in a larger studio, the bottlenecks are real.

I'd love to hear your thoughts on a few things:

What slows you down the most? (Asset creation, debugging, optimization, decision paralysis?)

What broke your last project? (A catastrophic merge conflict, engine updates, scope creep?)

What AI tools (if any) have actually made it into your pipeline? (Are you using them for brainstorming, coding assistance, placeholder assets, or avoiding them entirely?)

What do you find yourself Googling every single week?

Let's swap some horror stories and workflow tips. What's the biggest pain point on your desk today?

comments.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
comments.body:
What slows you down the most?:

Reddit

Now you, what

comments.author: ScutFarkush
comments.body:
I use AI to code and prototype features tell help me see if they are viable very quickly. Nothing has broke my project so far, but I am building in LOVE 2D and it is pretty forgiving. For my specific game, a weird roguelike, balancing and pacing dialing is taking the most time, ai is good to help gather data, but it does not seem to be good at balancing with that data, so I use it to collect data, as it can simulate runs very fast and then i tweak code based off of that.

asset creation take a bit of time also, but i am not using ai for that.

Making the game look good and appealing with shaders and screen transitions is also taking a lot of time

comments.author: rekansebangku
comments.body:
For me, the real pain point and horror is how AI brainstorming and planning can stress you out with too many options and ideas. You can easily get frustrated with the vision and roadmap that AI suggests because it explains all the possibilities and features that sound too good to be true. As a result, I get overwhelmed and often lose track of my own roadmap.   
  
Everything feels possible to implement, but in reality, it's just too hard. For example, a feature that sounds promising can end up taking way more time than you imagined. To overcome this, I usually brainstorm brainfart ideas with my AI buddy to give me some simple, stupid ideas to break up the stressful work. You can read the article here on how to do it, and for me, it works like a charm.

[https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/i-use-the-chatgpt-fart-prompt-whenever-im-stuck-and-it-somehow-works-every-time](https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/i-use-the-chatgpt-fart-prompt-whenever-im-stuck-and-it-somehow-works-every-time)

comments.author: West_Rutabaga3310
comments.body: brainstorming the different bits of ideas I have in my head. putting them into [gentube](https://www.gentube.app/p/world-builder?_cid=wb) does help a lot since it's so fast to create with

comments.author: mallcopsarebastards
comments.body: I'm a professional developer with some illustration experience so I suspect I have different pain points than others. The main thing for me is that I lose interest once all the engineering problems have been solved. When I get to the point of having to polish the game I get bored and move on.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Omg this is exactly my problem too

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: Weird how humans work. That's my favorite part. I despise scaffolding barebones features just to get the skeleton in. I feel like I have to see a feature completely implemented in order to truly know, "Yeah this is it!" Still retraining myself on that.

comments.author: Old-Promotion5528
comments.body: putting stuff together in unreal engine. lots of different items all needs their own settings, scale, value etc. Its just a lot of work and ai cant do it for me unfortunately.

comments.author: Apalala__
comments.body: the only limitation i have is AI credits and art assets.

comments.author: Wyabro
comments.body: I use a frontier model for planning and meta prompting my directions. Then I use various models in Cursor depending on the task for the actual coding and it works pretty great. As long as I do one thing at a time and check the output.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Visuals. And not even asset creation, as I do that by hand. I mean like.. If you want to lay out a UI, getting the AI to lay it out exactly as you want it takes more time then going in and creating the appropriate nodes. So that's fine, I just do that myself. But for instance my game recently needed an expansion on its procedural terrain. I don't know shit about algorithms required to get realistic looking terrain layouts and organic relief. I know what that looks like, but not how to do that. Well unfortunately AI can do it, but actually getting there is a very painful process requiring many... many iterations.

comments.author: AltruisticNostalgia
comments.body: Right now for me its animations. I want to do specific ones and the thought of going through that slog has me a little demotivated. I will be continue to polish and tighten up other things until then, but it's almost making me not want to touch it because of the time consumption that it's going to take.
